title: Xavier to Asia
hook: Francis Xavier sails to India, Japan, and dies on an island off China
carry: to the ends of the earth

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ignatius' cannonball, and a soldier who learned to notice in a sickbed. Your line was wounded into holiness. What did a stop in your day let you notice? Day eight hundred seventy-four.

So close he can see it. In a rough hut on a small island off the coast of China, a man lies with a fever. Through the doorway, across the water, is the mainland he has been trying to reach. Foreigners are not allowed in, and he is waiting for a trader who promised to smuggle him across. The trader doesn't come. The man in the hut dies there, far from the country where he was born, still looking at the shore. He had started out, long before, as a proud young student in Paris, sharing lodgings with an older man who walked with a limp. Today: Xavier to Asia.
screen: `A HUT ON AN ISLAND OFF CHINA.`

segments.voice: The older man with the limp was Ignatius. Francis Xavier was a gifted young Basque with plans for a fine career, and Ignatius, tradition says, kept asking him the question from the Gospel: "what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?" Eventually Xavier joined him, and became one of the founding Jesuits. Then, the story goes, when the man chosen to go east fell ill, Xavier was sent in his place, almost overnight. He sailed from Portugal on a Portuguese ship, around Africa, to Goa in India. He walked the fishing villages of the southern coast, and with helpers he put prayers and teachings into the local language. Accounts say he walked the streets ringing a small bell to call children to learn. Later he went on to Japan, where he found he had to change his ways: to learn courtesy, to dress for respect, to argue patiently with people who asked hard questions. Then he set his heart on China, and got as far as that island. In Acts, Paul and Barnabas quote the Lord's command to be "for salvation unto the ends of the earth." Xavier took that line literally. There's a harder side too. He traveled on the ships of an empire, and mission and empire were tangled together in ways that Christians in Asia, and historians, still talk about. Catholics honor him as a saint and a patron of missions. And he was not the first Christian in India: the Thomas Christians of the southwest coast trace their church to the apostle Thomas, long before any Portuguese ship. Asian Christians tell their own stories, which carried on long after the visitor was gone.

Here's the practice: hold Asia in mind. Settle, and breathe. Picture a map, and let your attention travel east the way Xavier's ship did. The coast of India, with its fishing villages. The islands of Japan. The long shore of China. Then let the map fill with people: anyone you know there, or whose family comes from there, a coworker, a neighbor, a friend. Let their faces come. If you pray, you can pray for them, and for the churches and peoples of Asia. If you don't, just wish them well, one by one. The bell holds the time.
Xavier. Francis Xavier, a friend of Ignatius, who sailed to India and Japan and died on an island off China, still trying to reach the mainland.
Your line: to the ends of the earth. Today, reach one person who feels far away from you, by distance or by difference, with a message, a call, or a kind word. Day eight hundred seventy-four.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Francis Xavier as a saint and a patron of missions, and in Goa, India, his remains are kept and venerated; Christians in Asia remember him as part of the longer story of their churches.

notes: Editor pass: hook opening varied (no longer another 'a ... on a ...' scene line); Acts 13:47 now attributed to Paul and Barnabas quoting the Lord's command, as the text has it; 'honest tellings' (used on day 870) and 'historians still weigh' (day 863) rephrased.
Claims rule: no dates, counts of converts, or ages.
Mark 8:36 KJV: 'For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?' (Matthew 16:26 KJV words it differently); confirm.
Tradition that Ignatius won Xavier over with this verse, and that Xavier replaced a sick companion (Bobadilla), given as 'tradition says' / 'the story goes'; confirm.
Ringing a bell to call children (from his letters / early lives), his change of approach in Japan, and dying on Shangchuan (Sancian) island waiting for a smuggler: confirm.
Mission and empire: framed as weighed by historians and Asian Christians, without ranking; a Keeper should confirm the tone. The Goa Inquisition question is deliberately not raised.
howItsDone: his remains venerated in Goa (Basilica of Bom Jesus); confirm.

Audit pass: the closing line could be heard as Asian Christianity beginning with Xavier; added the Saint Thomas Christians of Kerala (tradition traces them to the apostle Thomas) so the story isn't told only from the visitor's side. Confirm wording with a Keeper.
